title: Optimal Security for Correlated Sub-Key Distributions
summary: Known results cover one round and a constrained two-round case; characterizing correlated sub-key distributions that retain optimal security more broadly remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a $t$-round key-alternating cipher whose sub-keys may be correlated, determine which distributions of the sub-keys preserve optimal security against $q = N^{t/(t+1)}$ queries. Existing results address the one-round case and the two-round case under the constraint $s_0=s_1=s_2$, while the extension to more than three rounds and broader sub-key distributions remains unresolved. The open task is to characterize the correlated sub-key distributions, across the relevant round and parameter ranges, for which this optimal security threshold still holds.

scope.domain: Security of key-alternating block ciphers with correlated sub-key distributions.
assumptions: The known two-round result imposes the constraint s_0 = s_1 = s_2.
parameters: q: number of queries at the target optimal-security threshold
N: size parameter governing the target query threshold
s_0, s_1, and s_2: sub-keys constrained to be equal in the known two-round case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the correlated sub-key distributions, particularly for more than three rounds and broader parameter ranges, that preserve the optimal query-security threshold.

citations.label: Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys

progress.summary: The paper explicitly asks which sub-key distributions achieve the optimal query threshold after noting prior one-round and constrained two-round results. It reports partial progress for specific limited-independence key schedules while leaving broader distributions and parameter ranges unresolved.
citation_labels: Stefano Tessaro et al., Tight Security for Key-Alternating Ciphers with Correlated Sub-Keys
